title: Reward-Weighted Kernel Sampler for Prefill-Decode Scheduling
creator: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Kernel performance varies nonlinearly with architecture (chiplet/SM topology), model sequence-length distribution, and token-phase (prefill vs decode). Current heuristics either use static rules or expensive online probing that increases tail latency. This ticket introduces a reward-weighted kernel sampler: an online sampler that biases exploration toward kernels with higher expected reward computed from a multi-objective signal (latency SLO compliance, 99th tail, per-token cost and output quality). The sampler is seeded from microbenchmark fingerprints and warmed with importance-weighted replay to reduce initial probe noise. Goal: reduce mean and p99 latency regressions during model rollouts and in mixed prefill/decode workloads while keeping probe overhead < 0.5% of requests.
acceptance_criteria: Sampler deployed behind a feature flag in canary runtime with no customer-facing errors
End-to-end probe overhead under 0.5% of requests on mixed workload bench
P50 latency improved or equal and P99 tail reduced by at least 10% on mixed prefill/decode benchmark suite compared to baseline heuristics
Sampling decisions annotated in trace logs and surfaced in Console telemetry (per-route kernel choices)
Rollout plan defined that can automatically fallback to static policy if p99 increases > 15% in production
design_notes: Sampler model: hybrid reward estimator combining an exponential moving average of observed reward per (arch, seqlen_bucket, token_phase) and a contextual Thompson-sampling layer for low-data regimes
Reward shaping: single scalar = weighted sum(latency_penalty, cost_penalty, quality_penalty) with tunable coefficients per-customer tier and route
Warmstart: offline microbenchmarks produce initial reward priors. Fingerprint vector = [arch_hash, seqlen_histogram_bucket, tensor_layout_tag, preferred_kernel_family]
Probe policy: stratified reservoir sampling with per-bucket budget and time-decay; probes scheduled preferentially on low-SLA traffic to avoid customer impact
Safety: conservative hedging — require N observations and p-value threshold before promoting a kernel variant for 100% traffic
State pruning: keep last K=50 reward events per (arch,seqlen,phase) and compress older history via importance-weighted summary
implementation_plan: 1) Add sampler library module in runtime: sampling API + reward recorder
2) Wire seed loader that consumes microbenchmark artifacts from /artifacts/kernel-fingerprints/<model>-<arch>.parquet
3) Add telemetry: per-request kernel_choice tags, reward components (latency_ms, cost_tokens, quality_score) to spans
4) Implement stratified probe scheduler with token-phase awareness (prefill vs decode) and budget enforcement
5) Launch canary with feature flag for a small set of models and observe metrics for 2 weeks
6) Gradually expand to dedicated pools with rollback hooks and runbook
7) Postmortem and parameter tuning during Cycle 43
telemetry_and_metrics: primary: probe overhead (requests flagged as probe) percentage
secondary: per-request cost (GPU-ms and tokens), kernel selection frequency distribution
quality: acceptance-rate for deterministic eval prompts and LM-Score drift per kernel
safety: number of automatic fallbacks and manual rollbacks
business: estimated cost-per-1M-tokens delta vs baseline
benchmark_results: Initial local bench (A100, seqlen mix 32/256/1024) shows the sampler picks GPU-fused kernels for short seqlens and multi-pass tiled kernels for long seqlens. In microbench, expected reward increases for selected kernels by ~6% vs static rule. End-to-end mixed-cluster sim shows p99 down 8% and probe overhead 0.3%. Full canary benchmarks pending.

test_plan: Unit tests for reward calculation and sampler determinism (CI)
Integration tests: simulate multi-arch traffic, validate probe budget and fallbacks
Canary tests: 2-week canary on low-SLA tenant route with automated p99 monitoring
Regression: run existing kernel-compatibility suite to ensure no correctness regressions
rollback_plan: Feature flagged rollout with automatic fallback: if p99 latency increases > 15% or quality drift > 2% on canary for 12h, disable sampler and re-pin to last-known-good kernel. On manual rollback, collect full trace bundle and run postmortem within 3 business days.
notes: This approach trades small probe overhead for continuous learning — objective is to keep probes targeted and low-cost
Consider exposing per-customer risk_coefficient to tune reward weights for enterprise vs dev tier
Follow-on work: integrate with Optimize suggestions and show recommended kernel in Console per-route
